nodes.label: AppImage-bundled WebKit renderer abort
nodes.rationale: Reused id, same claim, re-confirmed on this host. The note reads finding F1 out of the plan doc and then verifies it: 'Confirmed F1: AppImage's bundled WebKitGTK renderer dies on this host; the same binary with system WebKit renders fully. So install pattern = extract the main binary from the AppImage, run against system WebKit.' The mechanism is the RUNPATH: inside the AppImage, $ORIGIN/../lib is the bundled WebKitGTK; extracted to ~/.local/bin it resolves to ~/.local/lib, which has none, so the system webkit2gtk-4.1 loads.
nodes.norm_label: appimage bundled webkit renderer abort

nodes.label: Escaped systemd scope app id for portal identity
nodes.rationale: Reused id, same claim. A terminal launch produced the log line that the portal would register the launch as 'zcode' from session unit 'app-zcode-124237.scope' rather than snipset-desktop. The fix the note lands on is the escaped application unit: systemd-run --user --scope --unit='app-snipset\x2ddesktop-<8 hex>.scope' --collect, run detached because --scope blocks until the child exits. The live session was then confirmed to live in app-snipset\x2ddesktop-7c4e91ab.scope.
nodes.norm_label: escaped systemd scope app id for portal identity

nodes.label: Linux Arch install runbook five invariants
nodes.rationale: Reused id, same claim. This session is where the runbook was written. The five invariants: never run the AppImage directly; install means extracting usr/bin/snipset-desktop into ~/.local/bin; never create or rename the desktop entry because its filename and Name=Snipset are load-bearing for the portal app_id; never write inside ~/.local/share/Snipset because that is user data; never leave a terminal-launched session running.
nodes.norm_label: linux arch install runbook five invariants

nodes.label: Tauri resource_dir() resolution API
nodes.rationale: Reused id, same underlying resolution rule, narrower emphasis. The note states it as: 'Tauri resolves resource_dir on Linux as <exe_dir>/../lib/<product>. With the GUI at ~/.local/bin/snipset-desktop that is exactly ~/.local/lib/Snipset/resources', which must hold the pinned whisper model, the cli/snipset sidecar, s2voices and ogg files. The operational consequence recorded here is that a missing or stale resource dir does not stop the app opening but does silently break speech and sound.
nodes.norm_label: tauri resource_dir resolution api

nodes.label: Resource tree diff decides what to replace
nodes.rationale: New id, no existing node covers it. The note's Step 4 hashes both resource trees and diffs them before touching anything, on the stated rule that both sides must have 13 files and that in this 0.6.852 update 12 were byte-identical so only cli/snipset was replaced. The instruction it draws: 'Never assume: copy whatever actually differs.'
nodes.norm_label: resource tree diff decides what to replace

nodes.label: strings marker proves frontend dist is embedded
nodes.rationale: New id, no existing node covers it. Stated reason for the check: 'No assets/index-*.js marker means the frontend dist is missing from the binary and the window will be blank regardless of WebKit.' The note calls this the check that would have caught the 0.6.851 blank failure in seconds, and cross-checks the expected marker against the release build log on the VPS. The actual marker found in the 0.6.852 binary was assets/index-C46sivMK.js.
nodes.norm_label: strings marker proves frontend dist is embedded

nodes.label: APP_READY precedes first paint
nodes.rationale: New id, no existing node covers it. Stated reason: 'The screenshot check is not optional. APP_READY main window ready is printed before the renderer has drawn anything, and the 0.6.850 session that failed earlier the same morning had produced exactly that line first.' Hence the three independent layers (log, resource resolution, pixels) rather than trusting the ready line.
nodes.norm_label: app ready precedes first paint

nodes.label: kioclient exec parses a desktop id as a URL
nodes.rationale: New id, no existing node covers it. Measured failure: 'kioclient exec snipset-desktop.desktop opened Firefox with the URL http://snipset-desktop.desktop! kioclient interpreted the argument as a URL, not a desktop file ID.' The companion trap measured in the same session is that kstart --application snipset-desktop.desktop blocked for 120s and started nothing. Both are recorded in the runbook as do-not-use.
nodes.norm_label: kioclient exec parses desktop id as url

nodes.label: Stale origin ref hides commit drift
nodes.rationale: New id, no existing node covers it. The VPS was three commits behind GitHub main while `git rev-list --left-right --count origin/main...HEAD` printed 0 0, because the VPS's origin/main ref was stale. Recorded as a trap: run git fetch before trusting a sync check. The shipped binary's provenance was therefore fe623848a, not main.
nodes.norm_label: stale origin ref hides commit drift

nodes.label: bun x tsc || true cannot fail the release
nodes.rationale: New id, no existing node covers it. The frontend build step is literally `bun x tsc || true && bun --bun vite build`, so TypeScript errors cannot block a release. The note records it as pre-existing and fragile, and separately confirms the specific run had zero error TS lines, so the observation is about the rule and not about that run.
nodes.norm_label: tsc or true cannot fail the release

nodes.label: Updater target and arch are separate query params
nodes.rationale: New id, no existing node covers it. The live endpoint answers 200 for ?target=linux&arch=x86_64 and returns HTTP 400 for target=linux-x86_64, which is the form the release tag uses. The note records this explicitly so a later check does not use the tag-shaped value and read the 400 as a broken deploy.
nodes.norm_label: updater target and arch are separate query params

nodes.label: Optional tunnel must not decide the exit code
nodes.rationale: New id, no existing node covers it. The design rule the note writes into start.sh: 'Only the dashboard decides the exit code. The tunnel never can.' Stated reason for the old behaviour being wrong: the unconditional TUNNEL_TOKEN=$(cat ~/.cloudflared/tunnel-token) under set -euo pipefail fails when the file is absent, and that failure lands before the health check ever runs, so a missing optional credential took down the whole launcher.
nodes.norm_label: optional tunnel must not decide the exit code

nodes.label: Tunnel guard checks binary and config file
nodes.rationale: New id, no existing node covers it. The guard is `if command -v cloudflared >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$CLOUDFLARED_CONFIG" ]`, and the skip branch names which half was missing. The note adds that the credential itself stays inside cloudflared: the launcher never cats a token file, it passes --config and lets cloudflared read its own credential.
nodes.norm_label: tunnel guard checks binary and config file

nodes.label: REPO derived from BASH_SOURCE works in worktrees
nodes.rationale: New id, no existing node covers it. Stated reason: the old hardcoded ~/terminal-log-intelligence is wrong in both the real checkout ($HOME/Proyek/terminal-log-intelligence) and any worktree ($HOME/Proyek/terminal-log-intelligence-wt/<name>), whereas REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)" works in both.
nodes.norm_label: repo derived from bash source works in worktrees

nodes.label: TLI_REPORTS_DIR left to the resolver
nodes.rationale: New id, no existing node covers it. Stated reason the launcher must not set it: TLI_REPORTS_DIR is used verbatim as the reports directory itself, and 'a wrong guess never self corrects'. The task's own preference is 'Prefer letting the resolver handle it: fewer places to get wrong', and dashboard/lib/paths.ts resolves $HOME/Dokumen/TerminalReports from user-dirs.dirs, confirmed by reading ~/.config/user-dirs.dirs.
nodes.norm_label: reports dir left to the resolver

nodes.label: systemd user unit PATH needs bun prepended
nodes.rationale: New id, no existing node covers it. Stated reason, in the script's own design notes: 'A systemd user unit has a minimal PATH, so bun is found through' the explicit prepend of $HOME/.bun/bin and $HOME/.local/bin. The matching test asserts the script references $HOME/.bun/bin for exactly this case.
nodes.norm_label: systemd unit path needs bun prepended

nodes.label: XDG state dir for pid files, not /tmp
nodes.rationale: New id, no existing node covers it. Stated reason: 'XDG_STATE_HOME is per user and survives a reboot, so the pids can still be found to stop a previous run', which /tmp did not give. The value is ${TLI_STATE_DIR:-${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}}, with TLI_STATE_DIR keeping the old /tmp behaviour reachable; the REVERT block still kills the pre-port /tmp pid files.
nodes.norm_label: xdg state dir for pid files not tmp

nodes.label: Execute the launcher under a stub PATH, not just read it
nodes.rationale: New id, no existing node covers it. Thirteen of the fifteen assertions are static; two actually run bash dashboard/start.sh with PATH set to a temp dir holding a stub bun plus /usr/bin:/bin, an isolated HOME and XDG_STATE_HOME, and TLI_PORT taken from Bun.serve({port: 0}) so the port is ephemeral. The note is explicit that it is not pretending otherwise and that cleanup is verified afterwards with pgrep -af Bun.serve and ls -d /tmp/tli-*.
nodes.norm_label: execute the script under stub path

nodes.label: bun absent must name bun as the only cause
nodes.rationale: New id, no existing node covers it. The task asked for a case with bun and cloudflared both absent asserting a non-zero exit is not merely the tunnel's fault. The note splits it instead: with a stub bun present the launcher exits 0 and prints the tunnel-skipped notice; with bun genuinely absent exit 127 is correct, and what is asserted is that the failure names bun and that no cloudflared, tunnel-token, or No such file or directory text appears.
nodes.norm_label: bun absent names bun as the only cause

nodes.label: Tighten the test rather than loosen the script
nodes.rationale: New id, no existing node covers it. Stated as the note's own call: 'Three test assertions were too naive and I tightened them rather than loosening the script'. Concretely, the pid-write check had to resolve the file-variable indirection, the guard check had to follow the -f variable back to its assignment and confirm it is the cloudflared config, and the exit-code check had to be scoped to three surrounding lines instead of anywhere earlier in the file.
nodes.norm_label: tighten the test rather than loosen the script
